subject: Model fit evals — post-call recap & parity thresholds
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Jessica Park <jessica.paygrid@paygrid.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Model fit evals — post-call recap & next steps

Hi Jessica — great to meet earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery:

What we heard
- Primary goal: replace PayGrid-Beta (your in-house baseline) for payment intent extraction and dispute classification while meeting existing latency/SLOs.
- Data: ~1.2M historical events; core eval set ~25k labeled examples across intents.
- Key metrics: intent F1, false positive rate on dispute detection, and per-message latency under peak.

Recommended experiments
1) Shortlist open models for initial parity evals: Llama-2-Chat-70B (quantized), Redmond-13B-Chat (opt), and a tuned Redwood-13B-mid quantized profile.
2) Run A/B runs against PayGrid-Beta on the 25k eval set with our prompt-set (attached) and your labeled subset.
3) Acceptance criteria (proposed): <=3% relative drop on intent F1 and <=2% absolute increase in false positives OR matching user-facing quality in manual review. Latency target: median inference <200ms p50 for single-request path (we can profile on your infra).

Deliverables & next steps
- We'll share a benchmark link with initial run artifacts and a short report — see attached baseline CSV stub.
- If you can share the canonical prompt sets and the 25k eval split, we'll run parity experiments and produce a model-by-model cost/latency matrix within 5 business days.
- Proposed meeting: 30-min sync next Wed (Mar 17) to review results and decide whether to move to a week-long A/B pilot.

Attachments: paygrid_benchmark_results.csv (placeholder), redwood_model_recommendation.pdf (summary).

Thanks — happy to adjust acceptance thresholds if you have compliance or audit constraints.

— Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com

From: Jessica Park <jessica.paygrid@paygrid.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 09:10:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Model fit evals — post-call recap & next steps

Thanks Lauren — that all sounds reasonable. A few quick clarifications:
- We can export the 25k eval split by end of day tomorrow.
- On acceptance criteria: I'm cautious about any >2% drop on intent F1 for our fraud detection path. Can we propose a stricter threshold for that specific intent class?
- Latency: our current p50 is ~120ms on PayGrid-Beta (prod infra). Anything above 250ms will be a hard blocker for the checkout path.

I'll loop in procurement separately for contract/po timing.

— Jessica
Jessica Park
Head of ML, PayGrid
jessica.paygrid@paygrid.com

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Jessica Park <jessica.paygrid@paygrid.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Model fit evals — post-call recap & next steps

Thanks Jessica — good call on flagging the fraud intent. Proposed update to acceptance criteria and a concrete plan:

Updated acceptance criteria (per-intent):
- Fraud intent: no more than 1.5% relative drop in F1 vs PayGrid-Beta OR manual review parity on a 1k sample.
- Other intents (routing, support triage): <=3% relative drop.
- False positives: <=2% absolute increase across the eval set.
- Latency: p50 <200ms, p95 <350ms on your target infra. We'll include quantized variants in the evals to hit latency goals.

Evaluation plan and artifacts
- We'll run the following models: Llama-2-Chat-70B-quant, Redmond-13B-optimized, Redwood-13B-quant-profile. For each model we will produce: per-intent F1, aggregated confusion matrices, inference latency distribution, and per-token cost estimates.
- Links: Drive folder with prompt sets and scripts: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcdExampleDriveLink
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/company/98765 (for tracking scope/next steps).

Next steps
1) You share the eval split + any redlines on the prompt set (ETA EOD tomorrow).
2) We run the first-pass parity eval and share results within 5 business days.
3) If parity looks good for the core intents (fraud routing + dispute classification), we propose a 1-week A/B on a small % of live traffic to validate downstream metrics.

Attachment: redwood_model_recommendation.pdf (contains recommended quantization profiles and cost estimates).

If this looks good I'll schedule the follow-up for Mar 17.

— Lauren

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Model fit evals — post-call recap & parity thresholds (internal)

Looping you both with a couple internal notes before we run the jobs:

Quick internal checklist
- Quality regression guardrails: we should include a second manual review pass specifically for fraud-edge cases and define an escalation path if the automatic parity criteria fail — propose a joint review board with PayGrid SMEs.
- Evaluation variants: run both int8 and nf4 quantized variants where available; capture memory and throughput so we can recommend Dedicated vs hosted profiles.
- Cost projection: include per-1M inference cost for each config (quantized and non-quantized) and an expected monthly bill estimate at PayGrid's volumes.

Also: watch out for label skew between your historical and the eval split — include a stratified sampling script in the Drive folder. I added a short script stub in the Drive folder (see link).
